title: Balanced sheaf tensor chain comparison with local generator normalization
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe [def-weil-size-convention], $R,S$ sheaves of commutative rings, and $\varphi:R\to S$ a ring-sheaf morphism. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], sheafified tensor and scalar extension [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], and scalar restriction $U=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. For every possibly unbounded cochain complex $P$ of $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] and every $S$-module sheaf $N$, write $N[0]$ for the complex concentrated in degree zero and $P_S^i=P^i\otimes_R S$, with differential $d_P^i\otimes1$. There is a chain isomorphism of $R$-module sheaves
$$a_{P,N}:\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes_R UN[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}U\operatorname{Tot}(P_S\otimes_S N[0])$$
for the signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. It is characterized, on the images of local presheaf-tensor generators in each degree, by
$$a_{P,N}(x\otimes n)=(x\otimes1)\otimes n,\qquad a_{P,N}^{-1}((x\otimes s)\otimes n)=x\otimes sn.$$
Both maps are morphisms of sheaves, including the scalar action through $N$ on $P^i\otimes_R UN$; the formulas use the sheafification units and do not identify sections of a sheaf tensor with tensor products of sections. The family is natural simultaneously in all chain maps $P\to P'$ and $S$-linear maps $N\to N'$. For a chain homotopy $h$ between maps of $P$, these naturality squares also commute with the induced degree-minus-one tensor homotopies, so the same family is natural on the homotopy category in $P$. No flatness or K-flatness assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product): sheafified balanced tensor formulas; their degreewise chain and homotopy extension

proof.text: First work with an arbitrary $R$-module sheaf $M$. Write $T_0(V)=M(V)\otimes_{R(V)}N(V)$ and $E_0(V)=M(V)\otimes_{R(V)}S(V)$, with the tensor restriction maps, and write $\eta$ for each sheafification unit. Give $T_0(V)$ the $S(V)$-action $s(x\otimes n)=x\otimes sn$. This respects the $R(V)$-balancing relation since $\varphi(r)sn=s\varphi(r)n$; the unit, product and additive action laws follow on pure tensors and hence on their sums. Restrictions respect this action since $\operatorname{res}(sn)=\operatorname{res}(s)\operatorname{res}(n)$. Thus $T_0$ is an $S$-module presheaf. Its $S$-module sheafification $H=T_0^\#$ has underlying abelian sheaf equal to the abelian sheafification of $T_0$. After restricting to $R$, its action extends the original $R$-action on $T_0$, so uniqueness of the action in module sheafification identifies $UH$ with the actual $M\otimes_R UN$. Likewise $E=E_0^\#$ is the actual $M\otimes_R S$, with $S$ acting on the second factor. These constructions define the required action through $N$, without any assertion that tensor sections are sectionwise tensor products.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), sectionwise tensor and scalar extension; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), unique sheafified action

proof.text: Set $K=E\otimes_S N$. On each object $V$ define $T_0(V)\to K(V)$ by $x\otimes n\mapsto\tau_S(\eta(x\otimes1),n)$, where $\tau_S$ is the pure-tensor map into the sheaf tensor. For $r\in R(V)$, the two balanced expressions agree because $\eta(rx\otimes1)=\varphi(r)\eta(x\otimes1)$ and $\tau_S(\varphi(r)e,n)=\tau_S(e,\varphi(r)n)$. The map is $S(V)$-linear for the action of step 1, since $\tau_S(e,sn)=s\tau_S(e,n)$. It commutes with restrictions: both orders take $x\otimes n$ to $\tau_S(\eta(\operatorname{res}(x)\otimes1),\operatorname{res}(n))$. The module sheafification universal property therefore gives an $S$-linear sheaf map $a_{M,N}:H\to K$. Restricting scalars gives the desired forward map on modules with its stated normalization.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), tensor balancing and units; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), factorization through sheafification

proof.text: Define a presheaf pairing $E_0\times N\to H$ by $\beta_V(x\otimes s,n)=\eta(x\otimes sn)$. It is well defined in $x\otimes s$ because $\eta(rx\otimes sn)=\eta(x\otimes\varphi(r)sn)$; it is additive in each input. It is $S(V)$-linear in each input because multiplying $s$ or $n$ by $t$ gives $\eta(x\otimes tsn)=t\eta(x\otimes sn)$, using commutativity of $S(V)$. It is natural in $V$: restricting this expression gives $\eta(\operatorname{res}(x)\otimes\operatorname{res}(s)\operatorname{res}(n))$. Apply the bilinear sheafification extension theorem with ring $\mathcal O=S$, presheaves $\mathcal F=E_0$, $\mathcal G=N$, and target $\mathcal H=H$. Here $S^\#=S$ and $N^\#=N$ by their sheafification universal properties. This supplies an $S$-bilinear sheaf pairing $E\times N\to H$. The sheaf tensor universal property then gives an $S$-linear sheaf map $b_{M,N}:K\to H$, with $b_{M,N}(\tau_S(\eta(x\otimes s),n))=\eta(x\otimes sn)$. This is the asserted inverse formula after restriction to $R$.

source.place: Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor), bilinear-extension hint; Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), displayed bilinear universal property

proof.text: The composite $b_{M,N}a_{M,N}$ takes $\eta(x\otimes n)$ to $\eta(x\otimes1n)=\eta(x\otimes n)$. Pure tensors generate each module $T_0(V)$, so equality on these tensors and the module sheafification universal property give $ba=1_H$. To show $ab=1_K$, the tensor universal property reduces the claim to equality of $S$-bilinear maps $E\times N\to K$. By uniqueness in bilinear sheafification extension, it suffices to compare them on $E_0\times N$. On $(x\otimes s,n)$ the composite gives $\tau_S(\eta(x\otimes1),sn)=\tau_S(s\eta(x\otimes1),n)=\tau_S(\eta(x\otimes s),n)$, as required. Additivity covers general elements of $E_0(V)$. Thus both maps are inverse $S$-linear sheaf morphisms; scalar restriction gives inverse $R$-linear sheaf morphisms as well. The same uniqueness arguments show that the stated generator formulas characterize them.

source.place: Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), uniqueness; Tag 0GMW (lemma-sheafification-tensor), bilinear-extension hint; Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), bilinear universal property

proof.text: Let $u:M\to M'$ be $R$-linear and $v:N\to N'$ be $S$-linear. The sectionwise tensor maps $u\otimes v$ and $u\otimes1_S$ respect restrictions and sheafify. Both composites in the forward naturality square, evaluated on $\eta(x\otimes n)$, are $\tau_S(\eta(u(x)\otimes1),v(n))$. Equality on pure tensors extends to $T_0(V)$ by additivity, and then to $H$ by uniqueness of sheafification. This proves simultaneous naturality of $a$ for arbitrary module maps $u,v$, with no requirement that $u$ be a differential or a component of a chain map. Naturality of $b$ follows by composing this equality with the inverse maps from step 4.

source.place: Tag 03EK (section-tensor-product), functorial sectionwise tensor; Tag 03CY (lemma-sheafification-presheaf-modules), uniqueness

proof.text: Now let $M=P^i$ for every integer $i$. In degree $i$ the direct-sum total tensor with $N[0]$ has only the possibly nonzero summand $(i,0)$. Indeed tensor with a zero object is zero: the sheaf tensor universal property identifies maps from $F\otimes0$ to any sheaf with the unique bilinear pairing $F\times0\to H$. The coproduct inclusion and projection for $(i,0)$ are therefore inverse (on all other summands there is only the zero map). Thus the left total has terms $P^i\otimes_R UN$ and differential $d_P^i\otimes1_N$; the right total has terms $(P^i\otimes_R S)\otimes_S N$ and differential $(d_P^i\otimes1_S)\otimes1_N$. The signed second differential vanishes because $d_{N[0]}=0$. Step 5 with $u=d_P^i$, $v=1_N$ says exactly that the maps $a_{P^i,N}$ commute with these differentials. Their inverses commute too, so they form a chain isomorphism. With $u=f^i$ and arbitrary $v$, step 5 gives simultaneous naturality for every chain map $f:P\to P'$ and $S$-linear map $N\to N'$. No sum has more than one nonzero term, regardless of the bounds of $P$.

source.place: Tag 012Z (definition-associated-simple-complex), signed direct-sum total; cochain complex and N[0] conventions preceding Tag 0113 (definition-homotopy-equivalent-cochain)

proof.text: Explicitly, a homotopy $h:f\simeq g$ has $R$-linear maps $h^i:P^i\to P'^{i-1}$ with $f^i-g^i=d_{P'}^{i-1}h^i+h^{i+1}d_P^i$. On the left total define $H^i=h^i\otimes1_N$; on the right define $H_S^i=(h^i\otimes1_S)\otimes1_N$. On a generator $x\otimes n$ the identity $F(f)-F(g)=dH+Hd$ is exactly $(f^i(x)-g^i(x))\otimes n=(d_{P'}^{i-1}h^i(x)+h^{i+1}d_P^i(x))\otimes n$. Additivity and sheafification uniqueness prove the identity as a sheaf map. On right-hand nested generators the same equation reads $((f^i(x)-g^i(x))\otimes s)\otimes n=((d_{P'}^{i-1}h^i(x)+h^{i+1}d_P^i(x))\otimes s)\otimes n$; tensor and bilinear-extension uniqueness extend it to all sections. Step 5 applied to the module map $h^i$ yields $a_{P'^{i-1},N}H^i=U(H_S^i)a_{P^i,N}$, and its version with $v:N\to N'$ gives the same compatibility with a change of $N$. Thus the tensor functors preserve homotopies and the natural isomorphism descends to chain maps modulo homotopy. The constructions and identities used only tensor relations and universal properties, so impose no flatness or K-flatness condition.

Proof: step 1 builds the S-action on T_0, which respects the R-balancing because S(V) is commutative; the uniqueness clause of def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification then identifies UH with M⊗_R UN. Step 2 builds a(x⊗n)=τ(η(x⊗1),n), which is balanced via η(rx⊗1)=φ(r)η(x⊗1), and gets it from the factorisation property. Step 3 builds b from β(x⊗s,n)=η(x⊗sn). I checked β is R-balanced and S-bilinear and that every hypothesis of lem-pc-sites-module-sheafification-bilinear-extension holds (O=S presheaf with S^#=S, N^#≅N, H an S-module sheaf); lem-pc-sites-sheaf-tensor-bilinear-universal then gives b. Step 4: ba=1 on generators, and ab=1 because the bilinear maps are determined on E_0×N; the identity τ(η(x⊗1),sn)=τ(η(x⊗s),n) holds. Step 5: naturality for any R-linear u and S-linear v. Step 6: F⊗0=0 by the bilinear universal property, so each degree has only the (i,0) summand and the sign term vanishes; the a's form a chain isomorphism with no boundedness assumption. Step 7: the homotopy h⊗1 needs no Koszul sign, and compatibility with a is step 5 applied to u=h^i. Edge cases M=0, N=0, φ=id, S=0, unbounded P all hold.
